root_cause.text: In the SpacemiT CCU mix clock driver (`drivers/clk/spacemit/ccu_mix.c`), `ccu_mix_trigger_fc()` had an inverted check on `common->reg_fc`, so it returned early when the frequency-change register was absent and skipped the required frequency-change trigger during cpufreq scaling.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (common->reg_fc) return 0;` to `if (!common->reg_fc) return 0;`, and the commit message says this “skips frequency change trigger, causing kernel panics during cpufreq scaling.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `if (common->reg_fc) return 0;` to `if (!common->reg_fc) return 0;`, and the commit message says this “skips frequency change trigger, causing kernel panics during cpufreq scaling.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the FC trigger path to skip updates when the FC register is absent.
intent_record.what: The conditional in ccu_mix_trigger_fc() was inverted: the function now returns 0 when common->reg_fc is false instead of when it is true. The subsequent ccu_update() call remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes the function so the frequency-change trigger register update is skipped when no FC register is present, and only proceeds when common->reg_fc is available. It prevents attempting a trigger operation in the unsupported case.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the FC trigger path to skip updates when the FC register is absent.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the same root cause: correcting the FC trigger path behavior when common->reg_fc is absent. That matches the inverted check in ccu_mix_trigger_fc() that caused the required frequency-change trigger to be skipped.

candidates.rationale: This inverted guard caused the function to return early when the frequency-change register was present/needed, preventing the FC trigger from being issued during cpufreq scaling.
This early return is the direct effect of the bad conditional and is the statement that skips the frequency-change trigger path, leading to the missed update.

vuln_statements.explanation: This inverted guard causes cc u_mix_trigger_fc() to return early when the frequency-change register is present, so the required FC trigger is skipped during cpufreq scaling.
This early return is executed because of the bad condition above and directly prevents the frequency-change trigger from being issued.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `ccu_mix_trigger_fc()`. The comment says FC is required after changing rates or reparenting: `Some clocks require a "FC" (frequency change) bit to be set...`. However the guard is inverted: `if (common->reg_fc) return 0;` means it returns early when the FC register exists, and only performs `ccu_update(common, fc, common->mask_fc, common->mask_fc);` plus `regmap_read_poll_timeout_atomic(...)` when `common->reg_fc` is absent. That is the opposite of the intended behavior and matches the root cause. There is no corrective handling in this function; the check is not fixed here.
